header_sentences: See Fallacy, Feel, Hear, See, Sensation, Sensory, Sensuous, Smell, Taste, and Touch.

contexts.text: Man's natural life (in the sixth state of regeneration) is delighted and sustained by the things which are of the body and the senses; from which a combat arises...
They perceived that they had been beguiled by the senses. Signified.
The evil (of all these Churches) has been that they believed... in themselves and the senses.
Men can now confirm the incredulity of the senses by scientifics unknown to the Ancients.
A Spirit is exactly like man as to the senses etc. AC 444.

They (then) acknowledge that it was the spirit which had sensated in the body... and therefore when the body is cast off the sensations live much more exquisite and perfect. Life consists in sense; for without sense there is no life; and, as the sense is, such is the life. AC 1881. AC 4622:3.
The whole brain is the Organic of the interior senses.
With such an inmost sense of Delight, that the fibre was as if nothing but joy...

They suppose that Spirits have not any sense, when yet they have a more exquisite sense than men; and there is superinduced on them by evil Spirits a sense almost as it were corporeal, which is much grosser.
External sight comes forth from interior sight, and this from a sight still more interior, and so on; and so with every other sense.
The objects of the external senses... were nothing to the Most Ancients... AC 1409.
They ought not to deny because it does not so appear before the senses.
During the life of the body the objects of the senses inflow...
Spirits and Angels have every sense, except taste, much more exquisite and perfect. Described. AC 1880.

These organic vessels (of the external man), which are to be the recipients, are not opened except by means of the senses, which, especially, are hearing and sight... They are opened by means of the senses through scientifics and Knowledges, and also through pleasures and delights...
The objects there, are adapted exactly to the senses of Spirits and Angels...
Spirits are in the enjoyment of all goods as to all the senses...
The objects which Spirits sensate are circumstanced in adaptation to the excellence of their sense.
Souls who long to see the glory of the Lord... are lulled as to the external senses... and then their interior senses and faculties are aroused...
In man's thought are innumerable arcana of knowledge and art... which never inflow through the senses... but through the internal man...
Things which it perceives by some external or internal sense.
The exterior memory is an Organic formed from the objects of the senses, especially those of sight and hearing, in the substances which are the beginnings of the fibres...
Believe only what they apprehend with the senses. AC 3024:5.
The first Rational is procured through the experiences of the senses...
They had supposed that the things of thought inflow through the external senses.
By the sense of his lower mind he can express in a moment...
This exterior good communicates with the external man... and makes the life in the external senses.
Spiritual heat, before their senses, is perceived as heat; but there is love in it...
For man thinks from those things which have entered through the senses.
It appears as if the objects of the world enter through the external senses...
Spirits of the exterior lamella of the dura mater are among those who have thought about spiritual and celestial things from such things only as are objects of the external senses.
Those who have worldly things as their end cannot withdraw the senses thence...
These purer or more interior forms... are those which present the internal senses... The interior Heavens correspond to these forms, because they correspond to their senses...
On the correspondence (of the Grand Man) with the senses in general. General article.

Sense in general, or general sense, is distinguished into voluntary and involuntary; voluntary sense is proper to the cerebrum, and involuntary sense to the cerebellum. In man, these two general senses have been conjoined, but still are distinct...
The organs of the senses receive for the most part fibres from the cerebrum; hence man has sense... But he has no sense of those parts which receive fibres from the cerebellum...
The Spirits who relate to the general involuntary sense. Described.
The quality of the operation of the general involuntary sense from the first times... and bow it progressed. Described. (See Involuntary.)
The general involuntary sense at this day. (See Involuntary.)
The Spirits who constitute the general voluntary sense. Described.
The external senses, etc. are the most general things (of man).
Sensuous scientifics are those which enter immediately through the external senses, and are perceived by the sense itself.

The external senses, which are five, namely, touch, taste, smell, hearing, and sight, have each a correspondence with the internal senses... The sense of touch in general corresponds to the affection of good; the sense of taste, to the affection of knowing; the sense of smell, to the affection of perceiving; the sense of hearing, to the affection of learning and also of obedience; and the sense of sight, to the affection of understanding and of being wise.
They marvelled that... they had sight, and the rest of the senses.

The Intellectual is nothing but an exquisite sense of interior things; and the higher Intellectual, of spiritual Things; hence the things of the Intellectual and its perceptions are called internal senses.

Those who have not reflected (suppose) that all sense is in the organs of the body, and therefore that when these organs perish by death, nothing of sense remains; when yet the man then comes into his veriest sensitive life.
Notions are taken from the things which are and come forth before the senses.
Whereas truth manifests itself, because it enters through the senses...
They are among the robbers who relate to the general involuntary sense.

The external senses, or those of the body, are five, namely, sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch: these constitute all the Vital of the body; for without these senses the body does not live at all, and therefore when it is deprived of them, it dies... and therefore the Corporeal itself is nothing else than the receptacle of the sensations, consequently of the life from them. The Sensitive is the principal, and the Corporeal is the instrumental... (Continued. See Sensuous.)

Every sense there is more exquisite and perfect because it is of the internal man set loose from the external; for the Internal is in a more perfect state because it gives to the External to sensate; but, when it acts into the External, as in the world, the sensation is dulled and obscured. Moreover it is the Internal which sensates the Internal, and the External which sensates the External...
Fourteen fallacies of the senses. Enumerated.
Hence the quality (of their affection of truth and of their faith) is there known to the open sense.
When scientifics are in the exterior Natural, they communicate immediately with the external senses of the body, and there repose and as it were rest upon them.

The tongue has been formed to all the sense of the fluent parts in liquid things... the touch, to the sense of cold and heat... and so on. As the external senses of man have been formed to all the image of the natural world, so his internal senses, which are those of his understanding and will, have been formed to all the image of Heaven, to the end that man may be, in particular, a recipient of Divine good from the Lord, as Heaven is, in general.
(A Spirit) has senses, namely, touch, smell, hearing, sight, much more exquisite than in the world.

It (appears) that the external senses, as sight and hearing, inflow into the thought, and excite ideas there; for it appears that objects move the senses; first, the external, and then the internal ones... but this appearance... is a fallacy... It is the internal sense, or the sense of the man's spirit, which sensates through the external sense, and disposes the external sensory to receive objects according to its bidding; and therefore the sensories... accommodate themselves in a moment to all objects according to their quality; which would not come forth in the sensories unless there were an influx from within; for all the fibres and little appendages... around every sensory or organ of sense, are determined in an instant in a manner suitable to the quality of the object; nay, a conformable state is infused in a moment into the organ itself. Explained. SE 4604.

Internal bliss... rarely puts itself forth... to the sense; for when man lives in the body, he sensates distinctly the things which come forth in the body, but very obscurely those which come forth in his spirit; for worldly cares... impede...

These (live) senses (from their correspondence with the Grand Man) have delights exactly according to the uses which they perform. The most delightful is the sense of conjugial love... Then follows the delight of taste... The sense of smell is a less delight... The delight of hearing, and of sight, are in the last place... These two serve the Intellectual, and not so much the Voluntary. HH 402. CL 68:end.
Many men many minds.
For man apprehends only those things which have been obvious to the senses: from these he has acquired a lumen...
Lastly, natural truths, which are conclusions from the objects of the external senses.
The inhabitants (of Saturn) relate to that in man which is the middle between the spiritual sense and the natural sense... AC 9107.
The Spirits of our Earth relate to the natural and corporeal sense... EU 89.
The Celestial of good and the Spiritual of truth are represented in the lower Heavens... before the very external senses of the Spirits and Angels there.
Yet the Angels have all the senses which man has, and much more exquisite.
For whatever man thinks, goes through the fibres from their beginnings to their ends, whence comes sense.
This bliss... is then revealed and let out into manifest sense, because they are in the spirit.

The spirit enjoys sensories and senses, when separated from the body, equally as when in it... In a word, all the life of sense which man has, is not of his body, but of his spirit... The reason the spirit sensated naturally when it was in the body, was through what is material adjoined to it; but even then it sensates spiritually at the same time, by thinking and willing.
That after death man is in every sense... in which he is in the world. Chapter.

Those in Heaven sensate much more exquisitely than when they were (here)... The difference of these external senses is like that between what is clear and the obscurity of a mist... but the rest of the senses, with the Angels, are not so exquisite as are the senses of sight and hearing, for the reason that sight and hearing are of service to their intelligence and wisdom, but not the rest: if these were exquisite in a like degree, they would take away the light and delight of their wisdom, and would introduce the delight of pleasures...
Just so great as are the perfection and excellence of the external and internal senses with the Angels, just so great is their imperfection with those who are in Hell.
As they (love themselves and the world above all things) they cannot pay any attention to anything except the things which enter through the senses of the body.
Few (spiritual things) can be produced to natural sense; for natural sense does not apprehend one thing out of thousands which the spiritual mind apprehends...

Man has five external senses, which are called touch, taste, smell, hearing, and sight. The subject of touch is the skin... this sense is in the substance and form of the skin... and is only an affection of it from the things applied to it. So with taste; this sense is only an affection of the substance and form of the tongue, which is its subject. (So with the other senses.)

(Thus) the affection of the substance and form which makes the sense, is not anything separate from the subject, but only causes a change in it... Hence it follows, that sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch are not anything volatile which flows forth from their organs, but are the organs regarded in their substance and form, which, while being affected, sense takes place.
For there are in the brain innumerable substances and forms, in which resides every interior sense which relates to the understanding and the will.
And all the senses of the body derive their perception from that of their mind.
For everything of the understanding and the will is first formed through the things which enter through the senses of the body, especially through the sight and hearing.
For all things which are sensated in the organs of the senses inflow from without, and are sensated in them: in like manner in the organs of the internal senses...

[155a]. [4]. Every male man has five senses... but we (wives) have a sixth, which is the sense of the deliciousness of all things of the conjugial love of the husband; and we have this sense in our palms when we touch the breasts, arms, hands, or knees of our husbands, especially their breasts, and also when we are touched by them...
I asked the husbands, Have you a like sense of conjugial love? They replied. We have in general, but not in particular...
Wives know their husbands' affections by three senses; sight, hearing, and touch.
Infants in Heaven... first grow in inclination to such things as please the senses of their body, and afterwards gradually to such things as affect the internal cogitative sense...
This (cold on the part of our husbands) we notice from the withdrawal of the sense from their eyes, ears, and body, at the presence of our senses.

Every love has its own sense: the love of seeing from the love of understanding, has the sense of sight... The love of hearing from the love of hearkening to and obeying, has the sense of hearing... The love of Knowing those things which are circumfluent in the air from the love of perceiving, has the sense of smell... The love of nourishing one's self from the love of infilling one's self with goods and truths, has the sense of taste... The love of Knowing objects, from the love of being circumspect and of guarding one's self, has the sense of touch... and the reason the love of conjoining one's self with a mate, from the love of uniting good and truth, has the sense of touch, is that this sense is the common sense of all the senses...
That... love and wisdom... inflow conjointly into the soul; through this into the mind, its affections and thoughts; and from these into the senses, speech, and actions of the body. General article.
Through their brains, the Spiritual World inflows immediately into the senses of the body (of animals).
There is such a cooperation in every sense...
What is sense without relation... to opposites?

It is according to Divine order that there be generals and particulars, and that both be together in every single thing... So it is with every sense of the body: with the sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch: and so it is with all the internal senses, which are of the mind.
That evil Spirits can, permissively, induce almost any sense, as it were heavenly...
There are two ways into the human understanding; through the senses and through Heaven...
SE 905. Hearing and sight belong to provinces of spiritual, and the rest of the senses, to provinces of celestial things.
On sense, and representations (there).
On the Spirits (of Mercury) who constitute those things in man which are called the internal sense. SE 1418. SE 1425. SE 1428. SE 1454. SE 1455. SE 3258.
On the interior sense of man. SE 1445. SE 1448.

Without sense there is no life, either corporeal or spiritual; and all sense relates to touch, even the more interior and inmost senses, as may be known to everyone even from the sense of sight and of hearing. SE 1719.
Correspondence of the Heavens as to degrees with the senses in the body.

That if man were in order he would still enjoy every sense which brutes do. - Some brutes possess a sense of knowing the way home... which sense is a general one in those who live according to order...
Man (even here) has not the sense of touch, and the rest of the senses, from the body; but from the spirit which is in it...

This is the cause of the corporeal touches which come forth only with those who have come recently into the other life. More subtle senses succeed, all of which must be referred to the sensation of touch, in order for them to be senses.
There are very many such in the world as reject spiritual things, because they do not apprehend them with the senses...
Every sense of the body has its own respiration, nay, its own place of respiration. Explained.
As the whole brain is the Organic of the internal senses...
Spirits have every sense except taste...
On the general natural sense. General article. (See AC 4325. AC 4329.)
Such become Spirits almost devoid of sense.
Spirits have been with me... also as to sense...
(Solifidians) are those who constitute the more general sense of Spirits...
On the Hell of those who take away all sense of civil, moral, and Christian truth and good.

There are two senses given to man which serve as means for receiving the things through which the Rational is formed, and also the things through which man is reformed, namely, the sense of sight, and the sense of hearing: the rest of the senses are for other uses...

None of the senses of man, namely, sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch, are in man; but they are excited and produced from influx. In man there are only the organic forms which are the recipients, which have no sense until something adapted flows in from without. It is the like with the internal sensories, which are of thought and affection, and which receive influx from the spiritual world, as with the external sensories, which receive influx from the natural world.
4. 2. Without correspondence and reciprocation, there is no life in sense...
2. 4. The will acts the first part in producing motions, and the understanding in presenting senses...
That the lungs act the first part in the senses, and the heart the second... (for) all the organs of the senses correspond to such things as are of the understanding. Enumerated.
